headline: Contact the certificate-transparency log the caller named, and refuse an options object that answers a second read differently.
summary: An options object belongs to the caller, so a property on it can be an accessor that returns one value to a check and another to the code that acts on it. The certificate-transparency log client read several options twice, and the two reads decided different things: a URL was approved by a presence check and the request went to another host, and a TLS configuration was approved by the trust-anchor check and the connection was opened under another. Every one of the client verbs now enters by the door `pki.ct.signSct` already used, which refuses an options object whose properties are not plain values rather than reading them twice, so the refusal arrives before anything is sent.

Fixed: `pki.ct.getSth`, `pki.ct.getProofByHash`, `pki.ct.getSthConsistency`, `pki.ct.getEntries`, `pki.ct.getRoots` and `pki.ct.addChain` read `opts.url` once to check it was present and again to build the endpoint. An options object whose `url` is an accessor therefore answered the two separately: the check saw the log the caller named and the request went wherever the second read pointed, which for a measured case was a different host entirely. `opts.tls` was read the same way, once for the trust-anchor check that refuses an unpinned log and once more for the connection, so the anchors that satisfied the check need not have been the anchors the socket used. Each verb now takes its options through one door at its own entry, and that door refuses an options object carrying an accessor, which is the rule `pki.ct.signSct` in the same module already applied. It also refuses an object that changes which options it carries while they are being read, since no set of checks can answer for one. A caller passing a plain object sees no change. The refusal is `ct/bad-input` and it happens before any request is sent, so a rejected options object cannot reach a log. Refusing an accessor on the options object is not the whole rule, because the door never inspects the members of a value, and a getter on a header name runs while the request headers are being copied. Three things it could reach from there are now taken before it runs. The URL is taken and converted to text at the same point, since holding the value alone is not enough when the value is an object whose text form names the host: a getter that rewrote an object-valued URL's `href` moved the request just as a second read would have. The TLS settings are flattened at that point too, and the anchor list is copied rather than shared, because a getter that emptied the pinned list after the trust-anchor check had approved it left the connection pinned to nothing. A caller that supplies options through a defaults object on the prototype chain is unaffected, including a function-valued `transport`. `pki.ct.fetchLogList` checked which option names it had been given and never entered that door at all, so its `url` was read once to parse and once to fetch, its `sigUrl` twice, and its TLS configuration once for the anchor check and once for the connection; it enters the same door now, over its own option set. Note that this is stricter than before: an options object with an accessor property was previously accepted, and the toolkit answered from whichever read it happened to make. Pass plain values.
